t: In front of you is Physical Energy, a bronze equestrian statue by George Frederic Watts. Watts was principally a painter, but he made sculpture too, and this was first cast in 1902, two years before he died. He meant it as a memorial to unknown worth, and described it as a symbol of that restless physical impulse to seek the still unachieved. There are four full-size casts: this one in London, and others in Cape Town, Harare and Compton, Surrey.
